races.name: Racing TV Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners_data.name: Yermanthere
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for the Easterby yard who has won over this exact course-and-distance on good ground; 11 days since last run is fine, but getting a clear passage late will be the challenge in a compressed finish.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form in fine style last time, landing a handicap at Ripon by a head off a mark 3lb below today's, and that tenacious display underlines his competitiveness at this trip; the trainer has a strong record at this course and the ground is in his favour.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sands
runners_data.note: T14 rate of 4/34 is modest but this horse has already won over 1m2f on good ground and is the only genuine front-runner in the field; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) notes it is operating out of role by being classed here as merely prominent — it is effectively a leader and should be assessed on that basis.
runners_data.comment: Struck over course and distance last time, getting up in the closing stages to take a handicap by a neck off a 4lb lower mark, and that late surge suggests the 4lb rise need not stop him; first-time tongue-tie added and the going here suits.

runners_data.name: Sandret
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old who has won on good ground and placed repeatedly over this sort of trip, but a natural rear-of-field type who has been pushed up to midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers in this field; the STYLE_FIT (0.93) discount applies, and Miss Hitchen's 5lb claim is the main compensating factor.
runners_data.comment: Well held on his most recent outing at Wolverhampton, running beneath his established level; he handles today's distance and conditions, but needs to find notable improvement to recapture the form that has brought wins in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Tees George
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a course-and-distance win on good ground to its name and solid recent turf form; Nicholls' T14 figure of 1/5 is quiet but the horse's profile suits this shape well and it should be travelling in a handy position throughout.
runners_data.comment: Filled fourth spot last time, beaten 3 lengths off a mark of 63 — just 1lb above today's — in a performance consistent with his capabilities; first-time cheekpieces arrive with the trainer in good form, and he has the ability to feature if producing his best.

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with 12 of 15 runs on good ground being encouraging, yet her true nature as a hold-up horse means the midfield berth shown on the map is not her natural habitat — she would ideally be further back; Alan Brown's T14 of 0/8 underlines a yard out of form.
runners_data.comment: At this course last time, beaten 3¼ lengths off a mark 1lb above today's but unable to sustain her effort after racing with too much enthusiasm in the early stages; the distance and going are familiar and she can last home at 12 furlongs in a steadily-run contest, but variable form makes her unreliable.

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: 51 days off the track is the obvious flag here, and while Ruth Carr is a reliable handler, the absence needs to be discounted; a prominent style suits this type of gallop and she has placed on good ground at 1m-1m2f, making her interesting if fit enough.
runners_data.comment: Well held at Leicester on his most recent start, beaten 9 lengths in a display well short of his better efforts; back after a break and today's surface suits him, but the mark continues to ease with good reason and a significant improvement is needed to threaten.

runners_data.name: Ephron
runners_data.note: The youngest horse in the field at three and the most credibly natural hold-up type available; a recent win on good ground over a mile suits the step up to 1m2f, though the inexperience of Miss Collier in an amateur contest is worth noting alongside a T14 of 0/10 for Tutty.
runners_data.comment: Acquitted himself well last time, filling second place beaten 1½ lengths off a mark of 67 — just 1lb below today's — and the going conditions suit him; the step back up to 10 furlongs is the main question, with his best form having come at shorter trips.

runners_data.name: Wrist Art
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old carry­ing a tv headgear combination and a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 — genuinely a horse that wants to come from the rear but is mapped mid-pack because the field is loaded with closers; only 3 runs from 15 on going this fast is a significant concern and James Owen's T14 of 10/57 gives little platform for confidence.
runners_data.comment: Finished third at Brighton last time, beaten 2¼ lengths off the same mark as today, suggesting he retains some form; tongue-tie and visor are both fitted for the first time here, and while he handles the trip well enough, inconsistency makes him hard to rely on.

races.paceDynamic: Shimmering Sands is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m2f Pontefract handicap and, with no genuine rival willing to dispute the lead, is expected to dictate at a comfortable, sustainable gallop on good ground. Tees George and Star Start will press from prominent positions, giving the leader a small group around it through the early stages, but neither is likely to force a genuinely searching pace. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Sandret, Princess Niyla, and Wrist Art are all natural come-from-behind horses who will be shuffled into midfield positions that do not fully suit their instincts, meaning their finishing kicks will be deployed from closer than ideal. With one uncontested pace-setter operating on a flat, galloping track and a steady tempo likely, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs rather than those relying on a late, clean passage from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shimmering Sands Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Shimmering Sands bowls along uncontested and sets a measured, even gallop that suits its natural front-running style.
scenarios.body: If Shimmering Sands bowls along uncontested and sets a measured, even gallop that suits its natural front-running style.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Tees George or Star Start travel smoothly in Shimmering Sands' slipstream and produce a sustained challenge from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If Tees George or Star Start travel smoothly in Shimmering Sands' slipstream and produce a sustained challenge from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is slow enough to bunch the field and a closer gets a clean run through to hit the line best.
scenarios.body: If the gallop is slow enough to bunch the field and a closer gets a clean run through to hit the line best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Shimmering Sands has a rare off-day or the honest early gallop causes it to tie up, leaving the race wide open in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: If Shimmering Sands has a rare off-day or the honest early gallop causes it to tie up, leaving the race wide open in the final quarter-mile.

watchPoints.text: Shimmering Sands has a clean passage to the lead with no rivals likely to pressurise it early — watch whether the gallop is genuinely honest or so slow that the field bunches and wipes out its advantage.

Sandret, Princess Niyla, and Wrist Art are all natural hold-up horses racing out of their preferred position — watch how freely they travel in mid-division, as any resistance early will cost them ground they cannot easily recover on this track.
Star Start is 51 days between runs for a handler who has been quiet; watch market moves at the off to gauge whether connections are confident she returns in peak condition.

Pontefract's long straight favours sustained galloping types over sharp finishers — watch whether Tees George can latch onto Shimmering Sands' quarters from the turn and grind past it rather than produce a single finishing burst.

Amateur jockey experience levels vary significantly here — Mr Henry Callan on Shimmering Sands versus 7lb claimer Miss Evie Lee on Wrist Art — watch whether any positional errors in the early stages disrupt the expected pace map.

races.name: Danny O'Neill Birthday 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Alfred Wincham
runners_data.comment: Landed his only start, taking a 4yo bumper at Down Royal by 5½ lengths, and brings that background to the Flat here; he acts on a sound surface over stamina trips and could make an immediate impact if that form carries over.

runners_data.name: Who's The Goat
runners_data.comment: A son of Decorated Knight out of a dam who showed fair ability at 10 furlongs, he is a half-brother to Golden Wolf, a useful performer at two miles or more; the trainer arrives in decent form, but making an instant impression as a debutant is never assured.

runners_data.name: Camelot Champion
runners_data.comment: A Camelot colt who is a full brother to a top-class performer at 10-12 furlongs, with his dam also having shown useful ability at a mile; from a strong yard, he looks well placed to make an immediate impression in what appears a modest field.

runners_data.name: Knight Of Storms
runners_data.comment: Made little impact on his only start, finding the early pace too strong in a maiden at Newbury where he was well held; improvement is anticipated but a significant step forward is very much needed to factor here.

runners_data.name: Sea And Sun
runners_data.comment: Gave a clear indication of ability on his sole start, finishing second in a novice at Ripon albeit beaten 11 lengths, and a break since should have him ready to progress; proven at around 11 furlongs on a sound surface, he merits respect if taking the expected step forward.

races.name: Darley EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Carnival Of Light
runners_data.comment: Ran with some encouragement on her sole start, finishing fourth beaten around 8 lengths in a novice at Ripon, and with today's distance and going both familiar, she looks capable of taking a forward step second time out.

runners_data.name: Stolen Kisses
runners_data.comment: Two starts have brought similar outcomes without threatening, her most recent outing at Ripon leaving the impression she is running to a limited level; a substantial improvement is required, though the trainer carries a strong record at this course.

runners_data.name: Capichera
runners_data.comment: Handled the step into handicap company well on her most recent start, going down by only 3 lengths at Nottingham off a mark of 80, and today's mile should suit a filly proven on a sound surface.

runners_data.name: Sedeirah
runners_data.comment: Beaten 6 lengths on debut at Haydock, unable to match the early tempo in a novice, but a pedigree that points to at least a mile and a top jockey aboard suggest she is capable of improvement; the trainer is in a lean spell of late.

runners_data.name: Take A View
runners_data.comment: Her debut effort has since been given a strong endorsement at a higher level, and today's drop back to a mile looks sensible for a filly proven on this going; a tongue-tie applied for the first time adds an element of the unknown.

races.name: Napoleons Casino Bradford Handicap

runners_data.name: Sir Paul Ramsey
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's hold-up specialist is well-suited to Good ground (two wins and a place from 9 similar-going runs) and returns after 61 days off; Jason Hart takes the ride on a horse whose back-of-the-field style is genuinely suited to this scenario only if Dovey Moon fires them along briskly.
runners_data.comment: Showed signs of a return to form when beaten 7 lengths here last time, a better effort than some preceding runs, and he handles today's distance and ground; off a 61-day break now, and he will need to produce more than that previous run to genuinely threaten.

runners_data.name: Dovey Moon
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, David Evans' four-year-old has won twice from eight Good-ground runs and arrives on a 17-day turnaround in form; PJ McDonald's ability to control tempo from the front is the single biggest tactical factor in the race.
runners_data.comment: Landed two races in his last five starts and his trainer is in good form, making him interesting; well below par last time where he was never involved, and today's step down in trip back to a mile is a question mark given his record so far on faster ground.

runners_data.name: Kaleido
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's prominent-style runner has strong recent course experience, winning over 7f on Good ground in his last five runs; Tudhope is a high-quality booking and the horse's six-from-eight record on similar going gives him solid claims if he can sit just off the leader.
runners_data.comment: Below his best when beaten 5 lengths at York last time, something of an underperformance, and more is needed to get involved here; his mark has been easing and he handles today's distance and surface well, while a top course jockey adds appeal.

runners_data.name: Selection
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's four-year-old has been placed twice at this trip on varied going and wears headgear; a natural front-runner/prominent racer who has the form to hold a stalking position behind Dovey Moon, though his recent string of 2-5-7-6-2 suggests consistency without always delivering the win.
runners_data.comment: Hit the line strongly at this course and distance last time, going down by the narrowest of margins off a mark just 1lb lower than today, and she deserved better; first-time cheekpieces, a course she clearly handles well, and a consistent placed record all point her way.

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's veteran — aged 11 — arrives on 14 days' rest with a strong recent record on Good ground (three wins and six places from 15 similar-going runs) and wears headgear; a genuine hold-up type by nature who has been bumped into a midfield slot by the redistribution — his true finishing kick is only triggered by a strong pace he hasn't yet been guaranteed here.
runners_data.comment: Ran to form at Wetherby last time, beaten just over 2 lengths off a mark a pound higher than today, and he loves to dominate from the front over 8f on any ground; first-time cheekpieces and a top course trainer add interest, though his recent profile suggests more is still needed.

runners_data.name: Sunriseontheboyne
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's four-year-old has struggled for form in recent starts (9-8-6-12-7) and none of those runs came on Good ground, making this a tough assignment; a hold-up stylist who has little winning form to draw on at this trip or on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard at Newcastle last time and was well beaten by 7 lengths, and he has not produced his best form since switching from Ireland; effective enough over today's trip on good ground, but an upturn in attitude is required to get involved.

runners_data.name: Jez Bomb
runners_data.note: Sam England's five-year-old is a genuine prominent racer by nature who has been displaced into a midfield slot because Dovey Moon, Selection, and Kaleido are better placed to claim the up-front positions; his headgear, 17-day turnaround, and two wins and five places on Good ground are positives, but racing out of his preferred role is a real obstacle.
runners_data.comment: Held up and ran to his level at York last time, though he tends to pull hard and that cost him there; first-time cheekpieces are a notable gear change, and while effective over longer trips the drop to a mile here may not be ideal.

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's eight-year-old carries the highest STYLE_FIT discount of this group, a natural prominent type shifted back in the map by the crowded pace positions; ten runs on Good going (one win, five places) suggests he handles conditions, but his advanced age and lack of recent top-three finishes (9-5-7-10-7 last five) make it hard to see him winning against this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Out of form and made no impression at Carlisle last time, staying in the rear throughout; first-time cheekpieces are a try, but a wide draw in stall 8 compounds the task, and it is difficult to make a case on recent evidence despite his versatility on any going.

races.paceDynamic: Dovey Moon is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner handicap over Pontefract's flat mile on Good ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, PJ McDonald can dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the front. Behind Dovey Moon, Selection and Kaleido are natural prominent types who will likely press into second and third, creating an orderly early shape rather than a contested scramble. The hold-up trio of Sir Paul Ramsey, Garden Oasis, and Sunriseontheboyne will be swept to the rear, giving them ground to make up in the straight. This field carries more prominent runners than the map can accommodate — Jez Bomb and Cosmos Raj are genuine prominent types who have been pushed into midfield because Dovey Moon, Selection, and Kaleido are most likely to secure the key positions ahead of them. A sustainable, unchallenged pace set by one horse strongly favours prominently-placed runners who can track the leader and pounce in the straight, with true hold-up horses facing a difficult task if the gallop is too steady to create a true late-race gap.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dovey Moon Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Dovey Moon is allowed to stride clear uncontested and sets a steady-to-moderate gallop that suits the prominent horses tracking just behind.
scenarios.body: If Dovey Moon is allowed to stride clear uncontested and sets a steady-to-moderate gallop that suits the prominent horses tracking just behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If Dovey Moon sets an honest gallop that strings the field out but begins to tire inside the final furlong, handing the race to the closest chasers.
scenarios.body: If Dovey Moon sets an honest gallop that strings the field out but begins to tire inside the final furlong, handing the race to the closest chasers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a strong-finishing closer, creating a late surge opportunity from the back.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a strong-finishing closer, creating a late surge opportunity from the back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Jez Bomb or Cosmos Raj push aggressively forward early, disrupting Dovey Moon's rhythm and turning this into a contested, fast-paced affair.
scenarios.body: If Jez Bomb or Cosmos Raj push aggressively forward early, disrupting Dovey Moon's rhythm and turning this into a contested, fast-paced affair.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Jez Bomb or Cosmos Raj attempt to push up alongside Dovey Moon in the early stages — if either horse challenges for the lead it will meaningfully increase the gallop and open up the race for Sir Paul Ramsey and Garden Oasis.

Dovey Moon's odds movement is key: if the market shortens significantly it suggests connections are confident PJ McDonald can control from the front, solidifying the prominent-horse scenario; a drifting price may indicate doubt about its jumping the gates cleanly.

Garden Oasis — aged 11 and mapped to midfield rather than its natural hold-up position — should be watched in the betting; if punters back it strongly despite its redistribution context, the market may know something about today's intended tactics.

Sir Paul Ramsey returns from 61 days off for Charlie Johnston, who has six winners from 44 runners in the last 14 days — watch for any market support that suggests the stable has the horse spot-on after the break.

Selection's headgear is worth noting in running — if the horse jumps well and settles smoothly just off Dovey Moon, it is in the ideal position to challenge; if it pulls or races keenly in the early stages, its chance diminishes sharply.

races.name: Pontefract Ladies Day Wednesday 5th August Handicap

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good ground at 5f including most recently, holds the key tactical position as the lone confirmed front-runner, and James Sullivan for in-form Ruth Carr (1/37 last 14 days is modest but the horse's own form is live); top-weight at 141lbs is worth monitoring over this sharp trip.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on his most recent start, below form by a wide margin off a mark just 1lb higher than today, and he needs to reverse that substantially; his trainer is out of sorts, and despite first-time cheekpieces his profile here is hard to warm to.

runners_data.name: Hover On The Wind
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's sprinter returns quickly (13 days) and has solid placed form, but is a natural hold-up horse who will find himself squeezed into midfield given the volume of closers in this field — his best work comes from further back than he is likely to get here.
runners_data.comment: Ran creditably at Thirsk last time, beaten just over 3 lengths off a mark 2lb higher than today, and he enjoys dominating at the front over 5/6f on a sound surface; tends to pull hard but is capable off this mark if he settles.

runners_data.name: Queen Sana
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's 3yo has been relentlessly placed (four seconds in recent form) on Good ground at 5f and 6f, and Daniel Tudhope provides a significant upgrade; as a hold-up type with a genuine finishing kick, she is one of the few closers whose natural style is not compromised by redistribution pressure.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in each of her last three starts, including a narrow defeat by three-quarters of a length here off a mark just 1lb below today's, and she handles this course and surface well; with a top jockey aboard from stall 4, she looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 7yo won his latest start over 5f on Good, carries a tongue-tie, and has good going-form figures (11/15 similar conditions); he is a natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield mapping slot by the volume of closers, so his ability to get a clear run in the final two furlongs will be decisive.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Beverley last time, finishing strongly to score by 1.5 lengths off a mark 6lb lower than today, and the top course trainer is a positive; first-time tongue-tie and blinkers accompany a significant rise in the weights, though, and more improvement is needed at this higher level.

runners_data.name: Knicks
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's 5yo filly has placed four times in recent runs but has not won on Good ground (0 wins from 4 similar-going runs); a genuine hold-up runner who will struggle to express that style fully given the crowded rear of this field, quick return at 13 days adds a small question.
runners_data.comment: Pulled too hard at Thirsk last time but still ran to his level, beaten only 2 lengths off this exact mark, and he handles the distance on good ground; the tendency to be headstrong is the reservation, but he has a genuine chance here if he can settle.

runners_data.name: Soca Star
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's 3yo has placed twice on Good at 5f and carries no headgear concerns; as a hold-up type with a clean record in similar conditions, she is not redistributed and her natural style is intact — trainer's 0/7 in 14 days is a mild negative flag.
runners_data.comment: Below her best at Redcar last time, beaten 3.5 lengths off a mark 2lb higher than today, and a return to her better form is needed; she handles the distance and surface well, her trainer is in good nick, and despite the wide stall 8 draw she has enough ability to get involved.

runners_data.name: Lucius Aurelius
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 4yo wore a hood when winning over 5f on Good last time and that headgear is retained; a genuine hold-up runner mapped to midfield simply because the field cannot park all its closers at the back — his soft-ground form is markedly better than his Good-ground figures (1W in 5 on similar going).
runners_data.comment: Third last time when returning to form, beaten 3.5 lengths off a mark 2lb higher than today, and a drop in the weights here could help; ran poorly at this track two starts back, and first-time blinkers are a significant gear change that could go either way.

runners_data.name: Without Flaw
runners_data.note: Tina Jackson's 5yo has consistent placed form on Good at 5f and 6f but finds herself among a group of true closers all competing for the same ground; she is the lightest-weighted runner in the field at 129lbs, and Jason Hart rides, though the trainer's minimal recent runners (0/2 in 14 days) gives little confidence.
runners_data.comment: Kept to form at Thirsk last time, going under by 3.25 lengths off a mark just 1lb above today's, and she is well suited by 5f on this going; her official rating has been easing and there is more to come if she can reproduce that level of effort.

races.paceDynamic: Betweenthesticks is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Pontefract handicap and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, she should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop rather than being burned up by a pace battle. The remainder of the field is stacked with genuine hold-up types — Hover On The Wind, Knicks, Dream Deal, Lucius Aurelius and Without Flaw are all natural closers who will be hunting her down from off the pace, while Queen Sana and Soca Star add further rear-ward pressure. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the back, meaning several of those closers — most likely Hover On The Wind, Knicks and Dream Deal — will be pushed forward into a midfield berth they don't naturally occupy, complicating their finishing efforts. With one horse controlling a fair but uncontested pace on Good ground over five furlongs, this race shape clearly favours a front-runner or a horse that can sit close to the pace and quicken from a handy position — a true, deep hold-up run from the back is structurally disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Betweenthesticks Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Betweenthesticks jumps cleanly and dictates a fair, uncontested gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: If Betweenthesticks jumps cleanly and dictates a fair, uncontested gallop from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp A Tiring Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Betweenthesticks goes too hard in front and the field closes her down in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Betweenthesticks goes too hard in front and the field closes her down in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Profit From Compromise
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed closers settle in mid-division and produce a late run that the leader cannot repel.
scenarios.body: If the redistributed closers settle in mid-division and produce a late run that the leader cannot repel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Entire Field
scenarios.trigger: If there is a messy break, significant traffic trouble, or an uncharacteristic early surge from multiple runners.
scenarios.body: If there is a messy break, significant traffic trouble, or an uncharacteristic early surge from multiple runners.

watchPoints.text: Betweenthesticks — if she gets a completely uncontested lead and the pace is genuinely slow, she could get first run on the entire field and prove very hard to catch over only five furlongs.

Hover On The Wind, Knicks and Dream Deal — all three are genuine hold-up horses who will be jostling for the same mid-to-rear position; watch for crowding and traffic trouble between them in the early stages.

Queen Sana — Daniel Tudhope's booking for an in-form yard is a notable market signal; she is one of very few closers in this field whose natural style is fully intact and not compromised by redistribution.

Lucius Aurelius — wore hood when winning last time on Good ground at this trip; if that headgear sharpens him early and he travels better than his redistribution slot suggests, he could outrun his odds from a handy position.

Weight spread — with Betweenthesticks carrying 141lbs and Without Flaw only 129lbs, the 12lb weight differential across the field on Good ground at 5f is significant and worth factoring into any late market move.

races.name: Wilfred Underwood Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Big Apple Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for the Easterby yard with Joanna Mason aboard, 11 days since last run (quick turnaround); placed twice in similar good-ground 6f races (0W3P sim-going) and the Pontefract trip-and-going profile is genuinely suited — this is a horse to respect at each-way odds.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Ripon last time, running to something close to his mark over the right distance and surface, and connections have a strong record in this event; the inconsistency in his recent profile is the reservation, but he warrants respect as a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Ideal Guest
runners_data.note: Harriet Bethell's seven-year-old is a natural hold-up horse pressed into the front-running role here solely because nobody else will go; 0/8 for the trainer in the last 14 days, 8 days since last run, and stepping back to 6f from 7f — the effort required to lead from the front at a trip on the sharp side of its range is a real query.
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who set a strong pace here last time but couldn't sustain it over 6f, going under by 2 lengths off this exact mark; first-time hood might help him settle better, but the wide draw in stall 8 and an inconsistent profile give reason for caution.

runners_data.name: Great Success
runners_data.note: Three-year-old from the Fahey yard with Oisin Orr up, back from 14 days; sit-off-the-pace style suits this scenario reasonably well but only 1 place from 4 runs on similar going (0W1P sim) and five placeless efforts at 6-7f on good ground recently make the form look regressive.
runners_data.comment: Encouraging fifth at Carlisle last time, beaten 2.25 lengths off a mark 2lb higher than today after a patchy run of form, suggesting a return to his better level; he handles fast ground over today's distance, and is the one to beat if he can build on that effort.

runners_data.name: Kyber Crystal
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' seven-year-old is genuinely a rear-of-field type forced into a midfield mapping here; wears a tongue-strap, 24 days off, and its best form has come over 5f on good ground (1W4P sim-going) — the step to 6f is a slight concern for a horse whose sharp-speed profile fits a shorter trip.
runners_data.comment: Below form at Thirsk last time, beaten over 6 lengths, and her recent record is unreliable; first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces suggest connections are searching for the right combination, though the trainer is without a win in the last fortnight and more improvement is required.

runners_data.name: Full Gas
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's three-year-old, 42 days off which is the longest break in the field and worth noting; a true hold-up runner nudged closer on the map, recently placed over 6f good ground (2nd at Wolverhampton), and if Ryan has freshened the horse up for a specific target this could be the one that goes close from a front-facing midfield position.
runners_data.comment: Usually held up and has shown solid form when things click over today's trip on fast ground; pulled too hard and was never a factor at Redcar last time, beaten over 6 lengths, and doubts persist about whether he always gives his full effort under pressure.

runners_data.name: Superstorm
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' three-year-old has raced mainly at 7-8f and the drop to 6f here is sharp; only 2 runs on similar going (0W0P) and its recent placed efforts have come at 7f-stamina trips rather than sprint finishes — the style redistribution and trip concern both temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Showed enough over 7f to suggest this level is within range, and the drop back to 6f with first-time cheekpieces is a potentially positive combination; below form at Yarmouth last time beaten 6 lengths on soft, and his current mark looks stiff, though conditions today may suit better.

runners_data.name: Lady Bouquet
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old mare is another genuine hold-up runner repositioned closer than natural on the map; 21 days since last run, best recent form at 5f on good ground (0W2P), and the 6f trip is a slight stretch — the low weight carried with Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is the main positive angle here.
runners_data.comment: A length off the pace at this track and distance last time off the same mark, and she handles any ground well enough; first-time cheekpieces are a minor positive, though a cold spell for her trainer tempers confidence and she remains yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Ganthorpe
runners_data.note: Lewis Chalkley (7lb claimer) rides the Easterby second string, 9 days since last run; recorded a win over 6f on good ground in recent history (1W1P sim-going) and has consistent placed efforts at this exact trip and surface — despite being a true hold-up type mapped to midfield, the trip-and-going match is the strongest in the field.
runners_data.comment: Clearly has ability at this mark and connections have a strong record in this event, and today's give in the ground suits his action; but he had a below-par effort last time out, failing to see out the trip when beaten 7 lengths, and a revival is needed.

races.paceDynamic: Ideal Guest is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 8-runner 6f handicap at Pontefract, redistributed to the front from a natural hold-up profile, meaning the early gallop will be set by a horse racing out of its comfort zone — pace will be present but is unlikely to be truly pressured or searingly fast on good ground. With Ideal Guest effectively dictating solo from the front, the tempo figures to be honest-to-steady rather than end-to-end gruelling, which on Pontefract's undulating 6f track (with its dip and rise in the closing stages) will compress the field somewhat and reduce the advantage for pure hold-up horses needing a strong pace to run into. The field is loaded with genuine hold-up types — Full Gas, Superstorm, Kyber Crystal, Lady Bouquet and Ganthorpe are all redistributed to midfield because there is simply no room for them all to sit in their natural rearward positions — meaning several will be forced to race closer than ideal, scrambling the typical hold-up dynamic. The tactical verdict is clear: horses who can race prominently or in a forward midfield position on a reasonable tempo, and who possess a quick finishing effort on good ground, are best placed — true closers dependent on a strong pace to peel off the rear are disadvantaged here.

watchPoints.text: Ideal Guest is setting the pace completely out of natural role — monitor whether Ethan Tindall (5lb claim) can hold a rhythm in front or whether the horse drifts or wavers early, as any erratic front-running would immediately compress the field and wreck the pace map.

Full Gas has had 42 days off — the longest freshness gap in the field — and Kevin Ryan runners returning after 6 weeks can show up sharply or flat; watch the market move closely pre-race as a significant drift or gamble here carries real informational weight.

Ganthorpe and Big Apple Jack are both trained by Michael & David Easterby, giving the yard two runners — watch which horse is supported in the market, as stable money on one over the other typically signals which is preferred for the day.

Kyber Crystal's recent form is entirely over 5f; the step up to 6f on Pontefract's undulating track (including a testing final climb) introduces a stamina query that David Allan will need to manage by holding the horse up — monitor whether it travels smoothly in the first half of the race or gets outpaced early.

Lady Bouquet and Superstorm are both lightly weighted and carry apprentice/conditional claims — if the pace is compressed and the race is set up for a sprint finish, low-weight hold-up types can spring surprises; flag both if the in-running sectionals suggest the pace has been slow early.

races.name: Wayne Conway Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Anificas Beauty
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at this trip on Good ground give her solid form claims, and jockey Cian Horgan (5lb claim) helps with the weights; a natural hold-up operator who gets to race in her genuine position here, and the recent course-going profile reads well.|
runners_data.comment: Landed back-to-back handicaps at Beverley, including over this course and distance, and clearly thrives on a sound surface; a 3lb rise looks within range for a mare in this form from a handy draw in stall 4.

runners_data.name: Hostelry
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's nine-year-old has been placed at this course and trip before and Joanna Mason knows the handler well with a recent winner for the yard; a true hold-up mare who can race from her natural position, though her win strike-rate (1W) on similar going is modest and she is vulnerable if the pace doesn't truly flow.|
runners_data.comment: Respectable fifth beaten 3 lengths at Beverley last time off a 2lb higher mark than today, and she handles any ground over a stiff mile; the wide draw from stall 9 is a concern, and a step up from recent form is needed.

runners_data.name: Daring Leader
runners_data.note: Christopher Kellett's five-year-old showed a flash of his best with a win over this trip at Southwell and has fair placed form, but he is a genuine hold-up horse whose true style has been displaced into a midfield slot here, meaning he will likely need cover that doesn't exist and a pace that may not materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Effective over 8-12f on a sound surface, with stall 1 on the inside rail a potential asset; but a response is needed after finding little when beaten nearly 10 lengths at Beverley last time, where he took the wide course.

runners_data.name: Nakatomi
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's four-year-old showed a strong placed effort at 8f on Good going last time and goes with the tongue-tie off; naturally a rear-of-field operator, he is mapped further forward than his racing style demands and Tom Eaves will need to find a way to produce him late in a race that may not have the tempo to suit.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Musselburgh last time having shown little, and first-time blinkers are a query; stall 8 is wide for this track, and a significant upturn in effort is needed to get involved despite his trip versatility on varying ground.

runners_data.name: Far Ahead
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey have a good 14-day record (5/61) and Oisin Orr is a shrewd booking in this grade; Far Ahead has posted placed efforts over this course and trip on Good going, but his true home is at the back of the field — slotted into midfield on the map, the tactical reality is that he could find himself caught between his instincts and the race shape.|
runners_data.comment: In good heart after consecutive second-placed finishes and beaten a little over two lengths off this very mark at Hamilton last time; suited by up to 9f on this going and consistent enough to be a genuine factor again from a handy draw in stall 2.

runners_data.name: Shark Two One
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, Jessica Macey's eight-year-old goes on the pace and headgear (cheekpieces retained) helps him focus; he steps up in trip from recent 7f starts and while his form figures are modest, an uncontested lead over an undulating mile on Good ground could flatter him considerably further into the race than his raw ability merits.|
runners_data.comment: Third in a classified race at Leicester most recently — a fair effort — and first-time cheekpieces suggest connections are trying to unlock more; effective over today's trip on any ground, but needs to reproduce that effort to be involved here.

runners_data.name: Elettaria
runners_data.note: John Wainwright's seven-year-old carries cheekpieces and has the benefit of a recent winning yard (T14: 3/7), and Paul Mulrennan is an astute partner; however, Elettaria is a hold-up type whose position has been shifted forward on the map — in a race likely to be run at a controlled clip, she may lack the finishing burst to make the redistribution pay.|
runners_data.comment: Third at Beverley last time, and fitted with first-time cheekpieces here, and well suited by today's distance and surface; below our top trio on figures, though, and a career-best effort would be required to get involved.

runners_data.name: Alice's Influence
runners_data.note: David Evans's three-year-old has a very progressive form profile — a win followed by placed efforts on Good and Soft ground — and PJ McDonald is a significant booking; her natural hold-up style leaves her in her correct position and her class edge over most of these, combined with strong similar-going form (3/8), makes her the most interesting genuine closer in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Well below her best when a distant fourth last time, beaten 13 lengths off a mark just 1lb above today, and a significant improvement in form is needed; a trainer in good shape and a drop to a lower weight are mild positives for a filly effective over today's trip on fast ground.

runners_data.name: Captain Bruce
runners_data.note: Andrew Crook's three-year-old is flagged as a horse who fades late, which is a serious concern in a race already unlikely to produce the strong pace that would bring hold-up horses into play; a genuine rear-runner pushed into a midfield map position, his tendency to weaken in the straight further dims his prospects in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Ripon most recently after showing little, and this good ground may not be his ideal surface given his best form has come on AW; off 32 days and ranked lowest of the nine on our figures, it is hard to make a case for him.

races.paceDynamic: Shark Two One is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, facing no meaningful pressure for the lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Pontefract's undulating mile. With just one horse intent on leading and the majority of the field holding up, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which will compress the race and make it difficult for genuine hold-up runners to generate the momentum they need to peel off the back and strike. The tactical verdict is clear: a steadily-run mile with a single uncontested leader heavily favours horses racing prominently or in the first half of the field, capable of tracking Shark Two One's rhythm before unleashing a finishing effort in the straight. This field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the map can physically accommodate at the rear — Daring Leader, Nakatomi, Far Ahead, Elettaria, and Captain Bruce are all true hold-up types pushed into midfield slots on the map, meaning only Anificas Beauty, Hostelry, and Alice's Influence are likely to actually claim their natural position at the rear, and even they may struggle to generate a winning run if the pace drifts too moderate.

watchPoints.text: Shark Two One controls the tempo entirely — watch whether Ethan Tindall (5lb claim) elects to quicken the pace before the home turn, as the decision to do so or not will determine whether hold-up horses have any chance of landing a blow.

Alice's Influence is the standout closer with genuine class and PJ McDonald aboard — watch her position two furlongs out; if she is still on the bridle in mid-division, she carries a serious late threat even in a slowly-run race.

Far Ahead, Daring Leader, and Nakatomi are all natural hold-up horses mapped into midfield — watch for early crowding as these three instinctively try to drop to the rear from positions the map shows them sharing, which could cause trouble behind Shark Two One in the early stages.

Anifacing Beauty's back-to-back wins at this course and distance on Good ground make her form highly relevant — watch whether Cian Horgan elects to hunt up to Shark Two One's quarters early, as doing so would put her in the prime tracking position this race shape rewards.
